post.title: Nearly 4 in 10 Run Out of Jobless Benefits Before a New Job
post.ig:
Nearly 4 in 10 people run out of unemployment benefits before they land a new job (NPR, Oct 11, 2026).
Layoffs are low: weekly jobless claims are near a 57-year low (Labor Department, Oct 8, 2026).
But the average stretch of unemployment was 24.8 weeks in September, and 1.9 million people (27.1% of the unemployed) have been jobless 27+ weeks (BLS).
Colorado pays up to six months of benefits; North Carolina pays up to 12 weeks, with a top check of $350 a week.
Sources: NPR, BLS, US Department of Labor.
